Recipes.Name: Negroni
Recipes.Notes: Stirring is gentler than shaking — keeps it crystal clear.
Recipes.Description: Equal parts gin, sweet vermouth, and Campari. Bittersweet and Italian.
Recipes.Tip: Stirring is gentler than shaking — keeps it crystal clear.

Steps.Title: Chill the glass
Steps.Instruction: Drop a big ice cube into a rocks glass and set aside.

Steps.Title: Build in mixing glass
Steps.Instruction: Add gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth to a mixing glass with ice.

Steps.Title: Stir for thirty seconds
Steps.Instruction: Stir gently until well-chilled and slightly diluted.

Steps.Title: Strain over fresh ice
Steps.Instruction: Strain into your chilled rocks glass over the big cube.

Steps.Title: Express and garnish
Steps.Instruction: Express an orange peel over the top, then drop it in.

Recipes.Name: Mai Tai
Recipes.Description: Trader Vic's 1944 original. Aged rum, lime, orgeat, orange curaçao.
Recipes.Tip: No orange curaçao? Cointreau works in a pinch, but you lose the bitter orange depth.

Steps.Title: Combine in shaker
Steps.Instruction: Add both rums, lime juice, curaçao, orgeat, and demerara to a shaker.

Steps.Title: Add crushed ice
Steps.Instruction: Fill shaker about two-thirds with crushed ice. The dilution matters here.

Steps.Title: Shake hard
Steps.Instruction: Shake vigorously until the tin is frosted — about twelve seconds.

Steps.Title: Pour unstrained
Steps.Instruction: Pour the entire contents into a tiki mug or double rocks glass.

Steps.Title: Top with crushed ice
Steps.Instruction: Mound additional crushed ice over the top to form a snowy peak.

Steps.Title: Garnish dramatically
Steps.Instruction: Slap a mint sprig and place it next to the spent lime shell.

Recipes.Name: Daiquiri
Recipes.Description: Three ingredients, perfectly balanced. The bartender's litmus test.
Recipes.Tip: Fresh lime is non-negotiable. Bottled juice tastes like regret.

Steps.Title: Chill your coupe
Steps.Instruction: Place the coupe glass in the freezer while you prep.

Steps.Title: Combine in shaker
Steps.Instruction: Add rum, lime juice, and simple syrup to a cocktail shaker.

Steps.Title: Add ice and shake
Steps.Instruction: Fill with ice and shake hard until the tin is too cold to hold.

Steps.Title: Double strain
Steps.Instruction: Strain through both shaker strainer and a fine mesh into the chilled coupe.

Steps.Title: Serve immediately
Steps.Instruction: No garnish — let the simplicity speak.

Recipes.Name: Old Fashioned
Recipes.Description: The original cocktail. Whiskey, sugar, bitters, ice — in that order, since 1880.
Recipes.Tip: Skip the muddled fruit. That's a 1990s thing, and we don't talk about it.

Steps.Title: Build in glass
Steps.Instruction: In a rocks glass, combine demerara syrup and Angostura bitters.

Steps.Title: Add whiskey
Steps.Instruction: Pour in two ounces of your chosen whiskey.

Steps.Title: Add a large ice cube
Steps.Instruction: Drop in one large clear cube — surface area matters.

Steps.Title: Stir to combine
Steps.Instruction: Stir gently for about twenty seconds to chill and integrate.

Steps.Title: Express orange peel
Steps.Instruction: Hold the peel over the glass and twist to release the oils.

Recipes.Name: Piña Colada
Recipes.Description: Puerto Rico, 1954. Coconut cream, pineapple, white rum — sun in a glass.
Recipes.Tip: No coconut cream? Full-fat coconut milk plus a teaspoon of sugar gets you most of the way there.

Ingredients.Name: Coconut cream
Ingredients.Sub: or full-fat coconut milk + 1 tsp sugar

Steps.Title: Combine in blender
Steps.Instruction: Add rum, coconut cream, pineapple juice, and lime to a blender.

Steps.Title: Add a cup of crushed ice
Steps.Instruction: About one cup — adjust to your preferred thickness.

Steps.Title: Blend until smooth
Steps.Instruction: Blend on high for about fifteen seconds.

Steps.Title: Pour into hurricane glass
Steps.Instruction: Pour straight from the blender into a chilled hurricane glass.

Steps.Title: Garnish tropically
Steps.Instruction: Pineapple wedge, cherry, paper umbrella. Maximum kitsch.

Recipes.Name: Tom Collins
Recipes.Description: Gin, lemon, sugar, soda. The original highball, 1876.

Steps.Title: Combine spirits
Steps.Instruction: Add gin, lemon, and syrup to a shaker with ice.

Steps.Title: Shake briefly
Steps.Instruction: Short shake — about eight seconds, just to combine and chill.

Steps.Title: Strain into highball
Steps.Instruction: Strain into a highball glass filled with fresh ice.

Steps.Title: Top with soda
Steps.Instruction: Top with cold club soda. Stir once to combine.

Steps.Title: Garnish
Steps.Instruction: Lemon wheel and a brandied cherry on a pick.

Recipes.Name: Jungle Bird
Recipes.Description: Kuala Lumpur Hilton, 1978. The bittersweet tiki drink that converts Negroni drinkers.
Recipes.Tip: The Campari does the heavy lifting — don't skimp.

Steps.Title: Combine in shaker
Steps.Instruction: All ingredients into a shaker.

Steps.Title: Shake with ice
Steps.Instruction: Fill with ice and shake until very cold.

Steps.Title: Strain over crushed ice
Steps.Instruction: Strain into a tiki mug or double rocks glass with crushed ice.

Steps.Title: Garnish with pineapple
Steps.Instruction: Spear a pineapple frond and a wedge through the top.

Recipes.Name: Paloma
Recipes.Description: Mexico's actual favorite tequila drink. Forget the margarita.

Steps.Title: Salt the rim
Steps.Instruction: Optional — rub a lime wedge around half the rim and dip in salt.

Steps.Title: Build in glass
Steps.Instruction: In a highball with fresh ice, add tequila, lime, and a pinch of salt.

Steps.Title: Top with grapefruit soda
Steps.Instruction: Pour in cold grapefruit soda almost to the rim.

Steps.Title: Stir gently
Steps.Instruction: One full stir, top to bottom, then garnish.
